findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "leave_event" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Gives up a guest’s spot or their place on the waitlist, or takes back their ask to join, with the `id` and `token` join_event gave. A spot goes to the first per…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: check_series, create_booking, share_booking_as_invitee, get_public_event, join_event, join_waitlist · Private data: get_available_slots, create_booking, get_booking, reschedule_booking_as_invitee, cancel_booking_as_invitee, get_shared_booking, join_event, get_event_guest, leave_event · Public sink: create_booking, share_booking_as_invitee, get_public_event, join_event, join_waitlist.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: check_series, create_booking, share_booking_as_invitee, get_public_event, join_event, join_waitlist · Private data: get_available_slots, create_booking, get_booking, reschedule_booking_as_invitee, cancel_booking_as_invitee, get_shared_booking, join_event, get_event_guest, leave_event · Public sink: create_booking, share_booking_as_invitee, get_public_event, join_event, join_waitlist

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
